ns2:course.label: Separation of Powers
ns2:course.description: Explores how the checks and balances built into the US Constitution affect the interactions between the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches. Addresses topics such as whether Congress is less productive during times of divided government; why some presidential nominees sail through confirmation, while others take years to be confirmed; and whether Supreme Court justices pay attention to the preferences of the President and Congress when deciding cases. Prerequisite: PS 101.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.
